text: Let us recap. In the Seebeck effect, a temperature difference between two junctions of different metals makes an e m f, set by the metals and the temperature difference. The thermoelectric series gives the direction: earlier to later through the cold junction. In the Peltier effect, a current heats one junction and cools the other, H equals pi I t, reversible, unlike Joule heating. The e m f follows a parabola, with the neutral temperature at minus alpha over beta and inversion at two theta n minus theta c. And a thermopile adds many couples in series to detect radiation.
